description:
## Why

Currently each stoa daemon instance is configured with exactly one block store backend. Operators have no way to:
- Replicate blocks to a second backend for redundancy (local fast + S3 backup)
- Migrate between backends without downtime (reads fall back to old while writes go to new)
- Tier storage (write to fast local store, fall back to cold cloud store for old blocks)

The IpfsBlockStore trait (4 methods: put_raw, put_block, get_raw, delete) is small enough that a composing wrapper is straightforward and composes with every existing backend without changes to any of them.

## What

Implement CompositeBlockStore wrapping Vec<Arc<dyn IpfsBlockStore>> with two config knobs:

**write_policy:**
- all — put to every backend (mirror/redundancy)
- primary — put only to the first backend (waterfall/tiered)

**read_policy:**
- first_found — try backends in declaration order, return first hit (waterfall/tiered)
- primary — read only from the first backend

This gives three useful operational modes from one type:

**Mirror** (write=all, read=primary): redundancy. Writes go to all backends; reads from the first. If primary fails, promote any replica by reordering the list.

**Waterfall/migration** (write=primary, read=first_found): zero-downtime backend migration. Configure [new-backend, old-backend]. Writes go to new; reads try new first, fall back to old for blocks not yet migrated. Run a background backfill job to copy old→new, then remove old from config.

**Tiered** (write=primary, read=first_found, first=fast-local, second=cold-cloud): hot/cold storage. Recent blocks served from LMDB or fs; older blocks fetched from S3 on cache miss.

## Design

- delete policy: delete-all in mirror mode; delete-primary-only in waterfall/tiered mode. Rationale: mirror must stay consistent; waterfall treats the secondary as read-only fallback.
- put_raw in write=all mode: compute the CID from the data once, then call put_block on all backends with the pre-computed CID so each backend does not recompute it independently.
- Errors in write=all: if any backend fails the put, return Err. Do not silently drop write failures on replica backends.
- Config: expressed as a [[backend]] array in TOML with a top-level composite.write_policy and composite.read_policy field. Single-backend configs remain unchanged (no array needed).
- Implement for both crates/reader/src/post/ and crates/transit/src/peering/.

## Acceptance

- CompositeBlockStore implements IpfsBlockStore
- Mirror mode: put goes to all backends; get reads from first; delete removes from all
- Waterfall mode: put goes to first backend only; get tries each in order; delete removes from first only
- Unit tests cover: mirror write-all, mirror read-primary, waterfall read-fallback, waterfall write-primary-only, delete semantics for both modes
- Config parsing accepts [[backend]] array and composite policy fields
- Single-backend configs continue to work unchanged
notes: The waterfall/migration mode is the highest-value use case for most operators. Consider implementing that first and deferring mirror/tiered until there is a concrete request.
title: CompositeBlockStore: run multiple backends simultaneously
